The eleven ratings for Bravida
Investment memo · Bravida Holding · BRAV-SE

Bravida (BRAV-SE): a real recovery that is already in the price; wait for SEK 115 to 120, or for proof of the data-centre margin

Written 22 October 2026, the day before Bravida's Q3 2026 report. Share price SEK 149.0; market capitalisation about SEK 30.8bn; two-year-forward P/E 16.3x to 16.5x. The forecasts are the Financial Analyst's model (“the model”); price dates, definitions and sources are in the end notes.

The verdict. Bravida is a good business in a real recovery, but its share price already includes both the recovery and a structural data-centre story. The most likely (modal) return from today's price is in the low single digits, inside a range of outcomes from about -25% to +20%. The risk/reward turns decisively positive at a share price of about SEK 115 to 120, or on evidence that the data-centre contracts earn 8% or more (DNB Carnegie, the broker that leads the market narrative, assumes 10%). Wait for one of the two, and use the next two quarterly reports to lighten holdings, not to add to them.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

1

Revenue is the predictable part of the case, and consensus already forecasts it. Organic growth moved from -7.7% in Q2 2025 to +9.0% in Q2 2026, with every country positive; the order book is 1.34 times installation sales; and about SEK 3.3bn of FY2027 revenue is contracted data-centre work. The model's revenue is within 1% of consensus through FY2027, so agreeing with the market on revenue earns no excess return.

2

The investment case turns on one undisclosed number: the margin Bravida earns on SEK 7 to 8bn of data-centre contracts. DNB Carnegie models 10%; the model and I use 5% to 6%, for the three reasons in the figure below. That one assumption, together with consensus's core margin of 7.0% (a level Bravida has not reached in ten years) against our 6.6%, explains the entire 8% to 10% gap between the model's EPS and consensus EPS for FY2027 to FY2028. Bravida reports no data-centre segment, so the first, blunt read on the contract margin will come from the Finnish and Norwegian segment margins in the Q4 2026 report (10 February 2027) and the Q1 2027 report (May 2027).

3

The earnings step is real but one-off, and the forward earnings the market prices stop growing from here. The model's adjusted EPS rises 17% in FY2026 and 14% in FY2027, then only 7%, 3% and 6% a year in FY2028 to FY2030. The step ends because the data-centre book completes in 2028 to 2029 faster than Bravida's central project office, which can run about two large projects at once, can refill it. By end-2027 the stock will trade on FY2029 EPS of SEK 8.80, which is lower than the SEK 9.06 of two-year-forward consensus EPS in today's price.

4

Against consensus, the risks are skewed down, and the order in which they arrive is unfavourable. The positive news arrives early and is small; the negative news arrives late and is large (figure below). Consensus FY2027 EPS of SEK 8.76 sits at about the 78th percentile of the plausible range of outcomes (SEK 7.0 to 9.0), so consensus already needs most of the good news.

5

Bravida's premium multiple depends on the company alone, so it offers no protection if the data-centre case disappoints. At 16.4x two-year-forward earnings, the stock sits at the 76th percentile of its five-year range and the 95th percentile of its two-year range, and 90% of the share's six-month price variance is specific to the company. Instalco, which shares the same Swedish recovery and the same sell-side momentum grade, trades at 12.9x. Bravida's three-and-a-half-turn premium over Instalco is the price of the data-centre story, and it rests on the same undisclosed contract margin as the earnings gap. The multiple is therefore a second bet on the contract margin, not a cushion.

6

The guideline fair multiple of 19.4x is too high for Bravida at this point in its cycle. Viewforth's rule assigns the guideline (the ten-year 90th percentile) from the dashboard's “Reinforcing” phase, but Bravida traded at 19x to 22x only in 2020 to 2021, with zero policy rates, a 6.5% peak margin and organic growth of +16% to +20%. My fair multiple is 15.5x (range 14.6x to 16.9x), which suits a non-moat installer with a widening data-centre capability, a strong balance sheet and a forward-earnings plateau. The model's +24.3% total return to end-2027 requires 19.4x; at 15.5x the total return is about +1% (range -5% to +9%), or about +5% a year to mid-2029.

7

The stock becomes an unusually positively skewed bet by one of two routes. The first route is price: at about SEK 115 to 120 (13x to 13.5x forward earnings), the modal 14-month return is about +24% against a downside of about -6%, a four-to-one skew. The dated negatives (margin pressure from Q1 2027, the cash trough in Q2 to Q3 2027, the spring 2027 wage round) and the sector's record (a miss at a re-rated technical-services company has cost 20% to 40% at Bilfinger, Fasadgruppen and Burkhalter) make SEK 115 to 120 a plausible price within twelve months. The second route is evidence: segment margins in February and May 2027 that show the data-centre contracts earning 8% or more, or a new award structured around Bravida's two-project capacity ceiling (a joint venture, or packages below SEK 1bn). That evidence would justify 16x to 17x and open the path to DNB Carnegie's SEK 173 target price.

8

Practical corollaries. For a holder, the Q3 and Q4 2026 reports will look strong on volume and cash for reasons already known, and they will reveal nothing about the data-centre contract margin. For an investor who wants exposure to the Swedish installation recovery alone, Instalco offers it at its own median multiple, with leverage of 2.6x as the trade-off.

Memo ratings: Thesis's Change Forces' Strength B; Foundations' Robustness C; Setups' Fit/Crispness C; Case Riskiness D (reasons in #13).

Grades: A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24. Each tile links to its topic; the reason for each score is given under the topic.

#1 Tailwinds in the operating environment; absence of headwinds

Demand is arriving on two legs: a cyclical construction recovery and a structural step up in data-centre work.

The cyclical leg is broad and has further to run. Nordic construction turned up from a two-year trough in Q1 2026, and the recovery now reaches across building types and countries (figure below). Veidekke's verified October update, besides its Swedish production forecasts, raised its Scandinavian contracting forecast to 7%. Because installation revenue lags building starts by two to four quarters, the 2026 recovery in starts will still be feeding Bravida's revenue in 2027.

The structural leg is a step change in data-centre work. Data centres were 1% to 3% of Bravida's revenue before June 2026. Since then Bravida has won SEK 7 to 8bn of data-centre awards, which now make up about 30% of the backlog and about 10% of FY2027 revenue. Swedish defence appropriations of SEK 175bn, a SEK 1,171bn national transport plan and the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD, transposed into Swedish law on 1 October 2026) lengthen the tail of demand but do not drive next year's revenue.

The headwinds are real, but they fall on margin, not on volume. On rates, the Riksbank has signalled hikes from November 2026 and Norges Bank is at 4.50%; through the two-to-four-quarter lag, higher rates reach installation revenue in 2028. On wages, the 3.0% to 3.4% expected for Swedish agreements is the relevant figure: SEB's “8%” is the rise in agreed minimum pay scales, which sit well below what skilled installers earn. Higher copper prices and long transformer lead times land on fixed-price contracts. On procurement, Bravida buys through a team of 50 to 60 people with no unified system, while the four wholesalers that hold 82% of Swedish electrical distribution pass costs straight through. On competition, Swedish tenders still draw about three times the historical number of bidders, and the next Nordic data-centre award will have two qualified bidders, not one, because Assemblin Caverion set up a Swedish data-centre business area on 31 August 2026.

Stress in AI-infrastructure financing matters more for future data-centre awards than for Bravida's contracted book. CoreWeave's bonds trading below 78 cents on the dollar show that financing for the next round of projects can crack. Bravida's contracted customers are better placed: Equinix and CPP Investments now own atNorth, and EcoDataCenter has EUR 600m of private credit and a SEK 1bn green bond. Green Mountain's financing of the Stavanger project is the least evidenced.

Inference. The external forces give Bravida its strongest volume set-up since 2022 and do nothing for its margin. The growth rate of the cyclical leg peaks around H1 2027: comparisons harden from Q2 2027, and the rate rises bite in 2028. The structural leg is contracted through 2028, concentrated in four customers and capped by Bravida's delivery capacity.

So-what. Forecast strong volume for H2 2026 to H1 2027 and a flat to slightly higher core margin, and treat 2028 to 2029 as the vulnerable window in which the cyclical slowdown and the completion of the data-centre book coincide. The model's revenue path in #6 (double-digit growth in FY2027, near zero in FY2028 to FY2029) has exactly that shape.

Strongest counter-case. The cyclical and structural legs could overlap for longer than the model assumes. Finland has 4.6GW of data-centre investment decisions due by 2029; DNB Carnegie sizes the Nordic construction market at SEK 400bn over 2026 to 2030; defence and transport budgets run for a decade; Swedish consumer confidence is above normal for the first time since 2021; and a Riksbank policy rate of 2.5% is still low by historical standards. On that view, 2028 is a second leg up rather than an air pocket.

What would change my view. Two signals together would push the vulnerable window out by a year: core (non-data-centre) order intake, found by subtracting the known awards from total intake, still growing in H1 2027, and a Riksbank that stops hiking at 2.25%. The opposite signal is core organic growth below 3% for two consecutive quarters.

Score: 62. Strong, dated volume tailwinds for the next four to six quarters, offset by cost headwinds that Bravida cannot pass on in its prices and by a rate cycle that has already turned against 2028 to 2029.

#2 Internally-driven corporate change forces; absence of problems

The clean-up of 2024 to 2026 is complete and dated.

The regional fixes are largely delivered. Denmark's EBITA margin rose from 0.1% in Q2 2024 to 5.1% in Q2 2026 and held there while Denmark grew 11% organically, which is the test that matters. Finland is closing weak branches, and its margin rose from 1.5% in FY2025 to 3.2% in Q2 2026. Sweden's three divisions merged on 1 January 2026, on time and within the SEK 90 to 100m budget; the merger saves SEK 65m a year (about SEK 40m inside FY2026, the rest in FY2027), and the last restructuring charge (SEK 10 to 20m) falls in Q3 2026.

The portfolio, the balance sheet and the control layer have been tidied. Bravida sold ABEKA on 1 April 2026 (SEK 472m of sales at a 7.6% margin) for SEK 208m of cash. The Stavanger arbitration award (about SEK 320m of principal plus SEK 145m of interest and costs) is final, because the appeal window closed in early September 2026. Bravida appointed a new CFO (May 2025), Head of Sweden (January 2026), Head of M&A (2026) and Head of Investor Relations (September 2026); it now requires the chief executive's sign-off on tenders above SEK 50m, has set up a risk council and has introduced randomised branch audits after the Region Skåne over-invoicing case. It also ran the first two buybacks in its history (SEK 100m each, executed at SEK 115.85 and SEK 141.79), and the board will “evaluate additional programmes continuously until the 2027 AGM” (annual general meeting).

The gaps matter as much as the fixes. The chief executive has been in place since 2015; the five financial targets are unchanged and undated; and the Capital Markets Day on 27 May 2026 added no figures (the “roadmap” that Morgan Stanley appeared to attribute to Bravida belongs to Securitas). There is no internal audit function across about 330 branches. Staff engagement is weak: the employee net promoter score (eNPS) is 14, against a target of 20 and Instalco's 31; unwanted staff turnover is 12.1%; and Denmark's injury rate is 9.8, against a group ceiling of 5.5. Acquisitions are at a trough (SEK 113m in H1 2026, against a 5% to 7% acquired-growth target), because private-equity-backed consolidators such as Nimlas and InstallatørGruppen outbid Bravida for the same targets. Twelve-month cash conversion is 77%, against a ten-year average of 99%.

The one genuinely new internal choice adds risk. Bravida's principal-contractor role on the atNorth data centre is its first at this scale, and Bravida delivers it with 80% subcontracted labour in its weakest unit, Finland.

Inference. The internal story has shifted from improvement to exposure. About three-quarters of the 2025 earnings recovery came from Denmark, and that gain is already in the earnings base. The improvements still ahead are modest but high-confidence, while the move into large projects raises growth and risk together.

So-what. Internal change is worth about 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points of margin and 3% to 5% of EPS by FY2027. It makes the earnings base cleaner and management more credible on cost. It cannot close the gap to the 7% margin target, and it introduces a failure mode that the old branch model did not carry: a write-down on a turnkey contract.

Strongest counter-case. Bulls read the same facts as a capability that compounds: a 70-person Special Projects office; a reference loop that produced four awards in three months; an eighth project for EcoDataCenter; follow-on service work at Meta's Luleå site worth 1.5 times the original build; and a balance sheet at 0.9x EBITDA (excluding leases) with SEK 2.5bn of undrawn facilities. That balance sheet could fund a SEK 1bn distribution, worth about +3% to EPS, which Deutsche Bank has publicly invited.

What would change my view. Upward: a dated plan from the company to reach a 7% margin, a buyback on a SEK 1bn scale, or acquired growth back above 3% a year under the new Head of M&A. Downward: a Finnish provision that includes atNorth, or a repeat of the municipal over-invoicing case (EY's warning that the problem “might be systematic” is still live).

Score: 50. Real, delivered and bounded fixes that are mostly already in the earnings base, set against a deliberate step up in project risk and against controls that are new, thin and untested at the new scale.

#3 Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile, management

The industry gives installers volume and withholds price. The Nordic multi-technical installation market is worth about SEK 180 to 209bn and has more than 25,000 firms. The top five firms hold about 18%, well short of the 30% this analysis uses as the threshold for a consolidated industry, and the tail of small firms bids at zero margin to keep crews busy. In installation, which is roughly half of Bravida's revenue, prices fall when volume falls, and main contractors manage their subcontractors “primarily on price”. In 70% to 80% of hyperscale data-centre projects the owner supplies the equipment, which removes the installer's procurement margin and procurement risk together.

Bravida's advantages come from its position, not from superior economics. Its positional advantages are density (about 330 branches and fast response times); a service franchise (48% of sales, on three-to-seven-year indexed contracts, with 91% renewal on contracts above SEK 5m and a net promoter score of 58); complex-project capability (about 200MW of data-centre projects since 2009, with 40 to 60 white-collar managers per site, matched only by Assemblin Caverion); and financial strength, which customers reward with “a risk-adjusted premium simply for being a financially stable supplier”. Its economics are ordinary: the gross margin has stayed between 14.2% and 15.2% for seven years and the EBITA margin between 5.2% and 6.9% for ten, below every listed peer (figure below). Return on equity is 13.8% (17.4% in 2021); capital expenditure is below 1% of sales; net debt is 0.9x EBITDA excluding leases; and cash conversion averaged 98% to 99% over ten years.

Management is an above-median team with a proven operating record and weaknesses in controls, targets and alignment. The chief executive has led Bravida for eleven years; the evidence on each side is set out in the figure below. His strategy (margin over volume, branch density plus bolt-on acquisitions, and complex projects for co-location operators rather than standardised packages for hyperscalers) is sound and tested through the cycle, but it is not bold.

Inference. Bravida holds a defensible position without an economic moat. Its margins will converge partially toward peers' margins through named regional fixes in Finland, Sweden and Norway, but will not exceed them, because the fragmented tail of the industry sets prices and Bravida's suppliers are more concentrated than Bravida is. Management reliably delivers bounded fixes and has never delivered the group margin target.

So-what. Model the core business at market growth with pro-cyclical, lagged margins; add margin only from named levers; and value the stock near its own ten-year median multiple, not at a premium to that median and not at the 34x of Comfort Systems, whose in-house prefabrication Bravida lacks.

Strongest counter-case. In the complex-project niche, the market is consolidating to two qualified players; “execution certainty now matters more than lowest cost” (Bernstein); and repeat customers negotiate rather than tender. That is how Comfort Systems lifted its gross margin from 17.9% to 24.1% in three years. Follow-on service work also turns each delivered data centre into an annuity. On that reading, Bravida is building a moat in the one segment that is growing, and group economics will follow with a lag.

What would change my view. A Swedish segment margin rising by more than the SEK 16m a quarter of merger savings can explain, which would mean real price increases in the core; a procurement system with a budget and a timetable; or a Finnish margin above 4.5% with atNorth inside it, which would show a premium for the principal-contractor role.

Score: 45. Average economics for a listed company and decent economics for an installer, in an industry that gives volume and withholds price, run by a good operating team without outlier standards.

#4 Conservative guidance; keeping the sell-side conservative; track record of delivery and upgrades

Bravida gives no short-term guidance, and consensus now sits above every one of its long-term targets. The five targets (growth above 5%, EBITA margin above 7%, cash conversion above 100%, net debt below 2.5x EBITDA, payout ratio of at least 50%) carry no dates. Management's informal aim, set in early 2025, to “reach or get close to 7% in FY2026” has slipped: the clean FY2026 margin lands at about 6.4%. All three operating targets were missed in FY2025 (table below). The hurdles in the long-term incentive plan (LTIP) are single-year stretch levels, not planning figures: the FY2026 hurdle is EBITA of SEK 2,144m against the model's SEK 1,935m, which implies only partial vesting.

The sell-side's numbers are the brokers' own constructions. One house leads: DNB Carnegie (Buy, target price SEK 173). One is an outlier: Deutsche Bank (Hold, target price SEK 106), whose organic-growth forecast the Q2 2026 report has already overtaken.

Bravida's delivery record splits by phase of the cycle. In upswings it beats on volume; twelve to eighteen months into an upswing it misses on project margin, as contracts priced before cost inflation meet higher costs (figure below). The latest volume beat, in Q2 2026, came after the chief executive had called it “too early to expect rapid growth”.

Inference. Bravida's targets are conservative on growth and aggressive on margin, and the company does nothing to steer the sell-side either way. Consensus has been rebased upward, so the chance to buy at a trough multiple of trough earnings (at SEK 75 to 80 in late 2025) has closed. The 2023 sequence of volume beats followed by margin misses is set up to repeat, this time as 2026-priced work meets 2027 costs in a new class of project.

So-what. There are no guidance-raise catalysts, so the quarterly reports will drive estimate changes: up a little through February 2027 on volume and a stale dividend estimate, and down from May 2027 on margin and cash. Reported FY2026 EPS of about SEK 7.6 to 8.1 (including the ABEKA gain and possibly the Stavanger interest) will print well above the SEK 7.20 adjusted consensus and will be called a beat, but the difference is purely one of definition.

Strongest counter-case. The chief executive's habit of talking volume down makes the next two reports near-certain beats on the line the market is currently watching. The model expects Q3 2026 adjusted EBITA of about SEK 420m (+23% year on year) against consensus of SEK 342m, in line with DNB Carnegie's SEK 417m, and a dividend of SEK 4.20 to 4.40 against consensus of SEK 4.00 would be a visible upgrade. Momentum could run on those beats into spring 2027, before the margin test arrives.

What would change my view. A dated plan from the company to reach 7%; or Q3 and Q4 2026 reports that pass all four of the model's tests (listed in #13), which would justify lifting the FY2027 margin forecast to about 6.7% and would close half the gap to consensus.

Score: 32. No guidance to lean on; a margin target missed for a decade, which consensus has now adopted as its forecast; and a delivery record whose next chapter, on the precedent of 2023, is a margin miss.

#5 Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out scope, feedback loops

Operating leverage is low, because about 90% of Bravida's cost base is variable. Production cost is about 84% of revenue, and management puts fixed costs at 8% to 9%. History confirms the low leverage: in FY2022 revenue rose 20% with a flat margin, and in FY2025 revenue fell 5% while the margin rose 0.6 percentage points. Today's incremental margin of about 11% (about 9% on the core business after the Swedish saving and the ABEKA disposal) comes from refilling the 4% headcount cut while crews in southern Sweden are still idle; it fades to the average margin as that slack is used up during 2027. As a result, margin matters about five times more than volume for EPS.

Bravida's pricing is nominal, not real. Costs pass through to prices with a lag of 9 to 12 months. Swedish contracts (47% of sales) are not indexed; Danish jobs longer than twelve months and service contracts are. On the company's own sensitivity of SEK 100m per 1% of payroll, the 2027 wage lag costs about SEK 25m in the base case, or SEK 60 to 80m if wage settlements exceed 4%.

Financial leverage and cost-out add little. Each percentage point on the loan rate moves profit by only SEK 15m. Buybacks of SEK 300 to 400m a year add about 1% to EPS, and each further SEK 1bn adds about 3%. Cost-out is the SEK 65m Swedish saving plus perhaps SEK 30 to 60m more by FY2028; Bravida has no procurement programme of the kind for which peers claim up to 150 basis points of margin.

Five feedback loops are running, and together they flatter 2026 to 2027 and penalise 2028 to 2029. The data-centre reference loop is the most important. It is reinforcing (four awards in three months) but has a hard ceiling, because Bravida can run only about two hyperscale-scale projects at once; Green Mountain and atNorth fill that ceiling until mid-2028, so new awards mostly start in late 2028. The customer-advances loop is a documented two-year cash cycle: cash conversion fell from 112% in mid-2024 to 77% as an earlier advance unwound; new advances and the Stavanger award make FY2026 cash strong (free cash flow at 105% of net income), and their consumption makes FY2027 weak (51%). The two earlier restorations (115% in 2019, 105% in 2024) support a return to 93% to 100% in FY2028 (chart below). The table sets out all five loops.

Inference. Revenue growth produces proportionate, not outsized, profit growth. Consensus applies a recovery-phase drop-through of 11% to 12% to the whole SEK 5.7bn revenue increase and assumes that data-centre work earns at or above the group margin. On the model's fading drop-through and a 5% to 6% contract margin, the same revenue increase delivers about 9%, and that difference is the SEK 170 to 230m EBITA gap to consensus. The loops make 2026 to 2027 look better than the underlying business, and 2028 to 2029 worse.

So-what. Do not pay for operating leverage. Bravida's EPS growth comes from volume, savings, Finland and a falling share count. The one mechanism that would make profit growth outsized is a 10% data-centre margin, and there is no evidence for it yet.

Strongest counter-case. DNB Carnegie's view that “20/80 subcontracting is not margin-dilutive” is right about the fixed cost base. The pricing signal from the National Institute of Economic Research could mark the first real price increase in a decade. Comfort Systems shows that complex work re-prices when execution certainty is scarce. And a SEK 1bn special distribution is a mechanical +3% to EPS that the board can deliver at any time with a quarter of its leverage capacity.

What would change my view. Swedish and Danish segment margins in Q3 2026 to Q2 2027 that hold drop-through above 12% after netting out the savings, or any company statement that the data-centre contracts earn above 8%.

Score: 38. A variable cost base that protects the downside and withholds the upside, no real pricing power, modest cost-out, and feedback loops that front-load the benefits and back-load the costs.

CashWorking capital at 19.5% of revenue in FY2026 (helped by Stavanger and new advances) and 20.0% from FY2027, as advances are consumed on SEK 3.5bn of extra revenue (an outflow of about SEK 860m); bank net debt stays below 0.8x EBITDA throughout.

Most of the EPS gain to FY2028 comes from the cycle, not from the data-centre contracts. Adjusted EPS rises by about SEK 2.5 from the clean FY2025 base to FY2028. About three-fifths of that gain comes from the cycle acting on the whole branch network, which is the most diffuse driver an installer can have; the data-centre contracts contribute only about 15% (chart below).

Against the past, the forecast is a step, not a compounding. From FY2019 to FY2025, revenue and EPS each grew 5.5% a year, and EPS was flat over FY2023 to FY2025. The model gives revenue growth of 7.2% a year and EPS growth of about 12% a year to FY2028, and 5.4% and 9.7% a year to FY2030. The margin improves about 70 basis points over five years, against a flat ten-year range, and never reaches 7% in the forecast period. EPS growth is double-digit for two years and then plateaus.

Two margin assumptions explain the EBITA gap to consensus. The model's FY2027 EBITA is SEK 2,176m, against consensus of SEK 2,370m: a gap of SEK 194m. Applying DNB Carnegie's published assumptions (10% on data-centre revenue, 7.0% on the rest) to the model's volumes adds about SEK 157m from the contract margin and about SEK 125m from the core margin (chart below). If the other brokers share DNB Carnegie's contract-margin assumption, roughly half the consensus gap sits in one undisclosed number.

The largest percentage gap to consensus is in cash, not earnings. The model's FY2027 operating cash flow is SEK 1.46bn, against SEK 2.51bn in consensus. Consensus assumes free cash flow of 1.2x net income every year; the model has 105%, 51%, 93% and 100% for FY2026 to FY2029.

FY2027 is the year to test hardest, and consensus EPS for it needs most of the upside case. The probability-weighted FY2027 EPS across the three cases below is about SEK 8.1, against consensus of SEK 8.76.

Confidence in the forecasts falls the further they move from contracted revenue.

Strongest counter-case. DNB Carnegie's base case is internally coherent: EPS of SEK 8.9 for FY2027 and SEK 9.7 for FY2028, and a 2030 scenario in which data centres provide 20% to 30% of EBITA and group EBITA reaches SEK 3.6bn at a 7.8% margin. If repeat customers negotiate rather than tender, 10% on the contracts is what the US template, Comfort Systems, earns, and the forward-earnings plateau disappears.

What would change my view. Upward: the four tests for the Q3 and Q4 2026 reports (#13), or Finnish and Norwegian segment margins from Q4 2026 that imply contract margins of 8% or more. Downward: a Q1 2027 report showing core drop-through below 8% with Finland back below 3%, which would take the FY2027 margin to about 6.3%.

Score: 55. Genuine double-digit EPS growth in FY2026 to FY2027 on a well-founded revenue path and a margin above the past, but a step-then-plateau shape that sits 8% to 10% below consensus where it matters.

#7 Scope for forecasts to lead to upgrades (guidance, sell-side, narrative) over 6 to 12 months

There is no guidance to raise, and the Capital Markets Day showed that none is coming. FY2027 consensus comes from six brokers: three refreshed since September, two stale since July and one outlier, Deutsche Bank (chart below). The live centre of FY2027 consensus EPS is therefore about SEK 8.7.

On the model's figures, estimate revisions peak with the Q4 2026 report and turn down from Q1 2027. The timeline below sets out what the model expects each report to show and the likely move in consensus EPS. The Q3 2026 report carries a risk of about 15% that FY2027 consensus is cut, and only on a Finnish or Swedish margin disappointment.

Inference. The odds favour lower estimates (figure below). FY2028 consensus (EPS of SEK 9.45, which assumes a 7.1% margin held while the data-centre book completes and wages reset) is more exposed than FY2027. The share of brokers recommending Buy is more likely to fall to 50% than to rise to 80%.

So-what. The market narrative is complete on the upside and silent on the three negatives that will decide the case. The fade in core drop-through is something nobody discusses as an open question; the data-centre contract margin is carried at 10% by the broker that leads the narrative; and the working-capital reversal is something DNB Carnegie warns about in its text while its cash forecast ignores it. A narrative that knows the upside but not the downside is the least favourable configuration for a new buyer and the most favourable for an investor waiting to buy at trough levels.

What would produce upgrades instead (about 20% probability combined). Data-centre margins of 8% to 10% visible through the Finnish and Norwegian segments from Q4 2026; Swedish margins rising by more than the savings explain (real price increases); a new award of SEK 2bn or more in H1 2027, structured as a joint venture or as packages the central office can run in parallel, which would refill FY2028 to FY2029; or a SEK 1bn distribution.

Strongest counter-case. The two stale July estimates and Deutsche Bank's SEK 106 target are obvious candidates to rise at the Q3 report, which would lift the mean of consensus without moving the median. Reported FY2026 EPS will print SEK 0.4 to 0.9 above adjusted consensus. And in this sector the market tends to reward volume beats for two or three quarters before it asks about margin, so momentum could carry the share through spring 2027.

What would change my view. Any of the four upgrade triggers above; or Finland at or above 4% in Q4 2026 with the Norwegian margin holding 6% as Green Mountain starts, which together would indicate that the contracts earn more than the model assumes.

Score: 30. Two more reports of small, already-expected upgrades on volume and a stale dividend estimate, then a revision cycle that turns down from the first half of 2027 toward a level 8% to 10% below today's consensus.

#8 Current momentum: guidance, sell-side, narrative, technicals, and the same for peers

Momentum is strong on every measure the dashboard pins. Sell-side earnings momentum is graded A: FY2027 consensus EPS is up 3% over one month, 3% over three months and 17% over six, and target prices are up 5%, 6% and 32%. Technical momentum is graded B: the price is 29% above a 200-day moving average that has risen in eleven of the last twelve months, relative strength is at the 95th percentile of the universe, and the twelve-month return is +68%. Valuation is graded D (the 71st percentile of the stock's own ten-year P/E range), and thematic momentum is graded D. The revision-momentum score is 11.

The same data show momentum cresting. The three-month return is +9.6%, after +51.8% over six months; the share of Buy recommendations has fallen 20 points to 60% (three Buy, three Hold); the mean target price of SEK 152 has reached the share price; one-month and three-month revisions are small; and the price of SEK 144 to 149 sits just below the 52-week high of SEK 152.8.

Bravida's strength is not shared by its sector. Instalco is the twin: graded B on technical and A on sell-side momentum, up 64.5% in twelve months, with a buy share of 86% and a revision score of 14, yet it trades at 12.9x, its own 46th percentile. The rest of the peer group is weak: Bilfinger has fallen 38% since its September profit warning, Fasadgruppen 56% and SPIE 8% (grades in the table below). Over the last six months the peer basket explains only 10% of Bravida's daily price variance (a beta of 0.65 to a basket that returned -3.5% while Bravida returned +53%).

Inference. Momentum is strong on every pinned measure and decelerating on every forward-looking one. The momentum is specific to Bravida: it came from the data-centre awards, the Q2 2026 beat, the Stavanger award and the buybacks, and the market has absorbed each of them. The share is waiting for its next company-specific driver, and the next scheduled drivers are volume reports that the market already expects.

So-what. Current momentum supports holding into the Q3 and Q4 2026 reports; it does not support buying here. Peers are weak as a hedge but useful as a signal. A good Instalco Q3 report (adjusted EBITA expected +33%) will not carry Bravida, whereas a bad one would read across to Bravida's Swedish core business, and core volume drives about 45% of the model's EPS gain to FY2028.

Strongest counter-case. Sell-side momentum of A, technical momentum of B, relative strength in the top 5% and a still-rising 200-day average make up the profile of a stock that keeps working for another two or three quarters. In this sector, recovery stocks typically re-rate 30% to 70% ahead of estimates and then move sideways while estimates catch up; Bravida's estimates have risen only 17% while its price is up about 90% from the low, so the catching-up may have further to run.

What would change my view. A Q3 report that lifts FY2027 consensus by more than 3% and restores the buy share above 70% would show that momentum has a second leg; a close below the 50-day moving average (SEK 141) after a volume beat would show that it is exhausted.

Score: 65. Top-decile momentum on the pinned measures, with every leading indicator (revision size, buy share, target prices at the share price, the three-month return) saying it has crested.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The revenue case is simple to track; the margin case is not. About 10% of FY2027 revenue is contracted and dated, the core order book covers eight months, comparisons are easy through Q4 2026, and Bravida discloses organic growth, order intake, backlog, mix and margin by country every quarter. By contrast, the one variable that separates the model from consensus, the data-centre contract margin, has no segment and no disclosure of terms, milestones, indexation or penalties. It will remain observable only through the Finnish and Norwegian segment margins, diluted by their core businesses: a Finnish margin of 4% in Q4 2026 could mean atNorth at 6% and the core at 3%, or the reverse, and the report will not say which.

The fragilities are concentrated, and the largest is a write-down on a turnkey data-centre contract. Its probability is 20% to 30% over 2027 to 2028, its cost SEK 100 to 400m, and under percentage-of-completion accounting it would arrive suddenly, after a quarter that looks normal. atNorth is the likeliest candidate: it is Bravida's first principal-contractor role at this scale, it sits in the unit that wrote down projects in 2025, and it adds a SEK 1.1bn ramp onto that unit's SEK 2.5bn of core revenue. The register below ranks all five fragilities by materiality.

Sudden, perception-driven risks could hit the share whatever Bravida delivers. The stock trades partly as an AI-infrastructure beneficiary, at the 95th percentile of its two-year multiple range, with liquidity of USD 10 to 13m a day. A cut in hyperscaler capital expenditure or distress at a Nordic data-centre developer would hit it; so would a Riksbank hike that breaks the “Swedish turn” narrative, a Bilfinger-style profit warning from a peer, or an over-billing story on SVT, the Swedish public broadcaster. A de-rating to the five-year median multiple of 12.9x would alone cost about 22%; the sector's record for a sentiment shock on a re-rated stock is -20% to -40%.

Bravida is cyclical, but its cost structure narrows its range of outcomes compared with its peers. It is a late-cycle, rate-sensitive installer in the most mortgage-sensitive developed economy, with 53% of sales in Norwegian kroner, Danish kroner and euros. Its own 2023 (a volume beat, then a 30bp margin miss and the Danish write-downs) is the median precedent. Peers fared worse: Instalco's margin fell from about 8% to 5.8% on cost inflation and fixed-price exposure; Bilfinger cut its 2026 margin guidance from 6.0% to 3.2% to 3.6% in one announcement; and Fasadgruppen's leverage forced a rights issue. Two structural facts protect Bravida. First, 90% of its cost base is variable, so a volume shortfall does not crush its margin as it did at Bilfinger, which employs its own skilled labour. Second, half of its revenue is indexed service work. That is why Bravida's 2023 miss was 30 basis points rather than 300.

Inference. Earnings drivers are diffuse, which supports confidence in the base case; risk drivers are concentrated in three places, two of them invisible until reported, which widens the range of outcomes around it. Around the model, the FY2027 range of outcomes (-14% to +11%) is roughly symmetric; around consensus it is skewed down. The timing is the asymmetry that matters: the largest single upside item can arrive in any quarter but is small, while the largest single downside item is more than five times larger and arrives without warning.

Strongest counter-case. Because the Green Mountain contract is cost-plus, most of the fixed-price exposure is removed from the largest contract. atNorth's civil works sit with YIT and Peab, so Bravida's risk there is coordination, not concrete. Two of the three data-centre customers are now well financed; no factoring flatters cash; and nothing in the model requires a strength Bravida has not already shown, except delivering the data-centre book at a package contractor's margin without a write-down.

What would change my view. Disclosure of escalation clauses on the atNorth and EcoDataCenter contracts, or a company statement of contract-level margins, would turn the range of contract margins from wide and invisible into narrow and trackable; a provision in Finland would confirm the downside tail.

Score: 40. Simple on revenue but opaque on the data-centre contract margin, with one binary fundamental risk and a multiple that would amplify any miss; the variable cost base and the service franchise are what keep the stock out of the bottom quartile.

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

The dashboard's rule places Bravida in the Reinforcing phase. The price is up 68% in twelve months, estimates are up 17% in six, sell-side momentum is graded A, and the narrative has moved from “cyclical installer in a trough” to “structural Nordic AI-infrastructure enabler with self-help”.

The marks of a phase ending are also present. Besides the cresting momentum set out in #8, the narrative has no dynamics left to discover on the upside and three to discover on the downside; forward EPS plateaus from FY2028; and the first dated tests of the margin thesis (the Q1 and Q2 2027 reports) are still six to nine months away.

The sector's precedent says the market does not pay for data-centre exposure as a theme. SPIE, with a data-centre and grid narrative, 70% service revenue and a 7.6% margin, trades at 11.7x and has not re-rated; Instalco, with the same Swedish recovery and no data-centre story, trades at its median. European investors have paid Bravida for a step change in growth, not for the theme. If the growth step ends in 2028, the SPIE precedent says Bravida's premium disappears.

Inference. Bravida is in late Reinforcing, tipping toward Stalling in the first half of 2027. The reinforcing mechanism (volume beats plus new awards) has two more quarters to run; the stalling mechanism (margin fade, cash trough, forward-EPS plateau, and a two-bidder market for the next award) is dated and arrives afterwards. On the model's path, the market's “structural” claim is tested in 2027 and does not show in the numbers before 2028. That describes a stall rather than a collapse: the business keeps growing earnings at a mid-single-digit rate, but the multiple loses its reason to sit at the 95th percentile.

So-what. The phase argues for the lower part of the multiple range, not the top, because the forecasts are uncertain and momentum is cresting. It also sets the playbook: the stock turns up again either at a trough multiple with earnings intact (the price route) or at the current multiple with the contract margin proven (the evidence route).

Strongest counter-case. The Reinforcing phase could run longer. The next two reports are set up to beat, the consensus dividend is stale, and a fifth or sixth data-centre award in H1 2027 (the pipeline includes atNorth's Haugaland, Sollefteå and Salo sites and EcoDataCenter's third campus) would reopen the Thesis Broadening phase before the margin test arrives. DNB Carnegie's bull case of SEK 275 rests on exactly that.

What would change my view. The two triggers shown in the phase diagram above: a capacity-structured award or proven contract margins of 8% or more would move the stock up to Thesis Broadening, and weak core growth with a Finnish provision would move it straight to Collapsing.

Score: 45. A Reinforcing phase whose reinforcing drivers have been absorbed and whose dated tests fall in the first half of 2027, with forward earnings already flattening.

#11 The fair multiple

Today's multiple is high against the stock's own history but below the guideline fair multiple. Over ten years (outliers removed), the two-year-forward P/E has had a 10th percentile of 10.9x, a median of 14.6x, a 75th percentile of 16.9x and a 90th percentile of 19.4x. Today's 16.3x to 16.5x is the 71st percentile of ten years, the 76th of five and the 95th of two. The guideline fair multiple, set by Viewforth's rule for the Reinforcing phase, is 19.38x, 19% above today's.

The 19x to 22x band needs conditions that no longer hold. Bravida traded there only from mid-2020 to end-2021 (table below), then de-rated to 10x to 12x through 2023 to 2025 as margins fell and rates rose. The US ten-year yield is about 5.1% today, and, as Viewforth's environment digest puts it, the current rate regime refuses re-ratings.

Peers and brokers anchor lower. Instalco trades at 12.9x (its own 46th percentile) and SPIE at 11.7x; Bilfinger trades at about 6.5x forward EV/EBIT after its warning; and Burkhalter trades at 18x on 1% to 3% growth, for which its shares have fallen 28% in six months. DNB Carnegie's SEK 173 target uses 15x FY2027 EV/EBITA, against a 13.5x historical average; Deutsche Bank's trough reference is 11.3x EV/EBITA.

Inference. Bravida's profile does not earn the 90th percentile. A business that grows about 7% a year through the cycle, with mid-teens returns on limited reinvestment, no pricing power and a flat ten-year margin range, merits its own median. A widening capability in complex projects, the strongest balance sheet in its peer group, a 48% indexed service franchise and a cleaner base after the 2024 to 2026 fixes earn some premium to that median. A forward-earnings plateau from FY2028 and a cresting phase argue against going to the top of the range. My fair multiple is therefore 15.5x, within a range from 14.6x (the median, if the data-centre contracts earn only a package contractor's margin and the book is not refilled) to 16.9x (the 75th percentile, if the contracts earn 8% or more and the refill is visible). The guideline's 19.4x is what the stock would deserve if DNB Carnegie's 10% margin and 2030 scenario were demonstrated, in a lower-rate regime; neither condition holds today.

So-what. At 16.4x, the stock is about 6% above my central fair multiple and 16% below the guideline. The choice between the two multiples is the largest single determinant of the return, because 90% of the share's price variance is company-specific, and it rests on the same undisclosed contract margin as the earnings gap. Treat the multiple as correlated with the earnings bet, not as diversification from it.

Strongest counter-case. Phase-based valuation is designed to resist exactly this kind of mean-reversion instinct: in the Reinforcing phase the market pays the top of the range, and the discipline is to let it. Bravida reached 19x to 22x once before on a growth step, and FY2026 to FY2027 is a growth step. The dividend yield at SEK 4.20 is 2.9% and rising, and a SEK 1bn distribution would signal the board's confidence in the cash cycle.

What would change my view. Up to 17x to 19x: contract margins proven above 8% in the 2027 segment data, a refill award in H1 2027, or a dated plan from the company to reach a 7% margin. Down to 13x to 14x: a Finnish provision, FY2027 cash conversion printing at the model's 51% without a new prepaid award, or core organic growth below 3% for two quarters.

Score: 35. The stock trades above my fair multiple (15.5x) and well below the phase guideline (19.4x); the guideline needs a margin that Bravida has never reported and a rate regime that no longer exists.

#12 Total shareholder return (DuPont): earnings growth, change in multiple, dividends

The model's return depends on the share reaching the 19.38x guideline multiple. From SEK 144.40, with 19.38x reached at the 18-month horizon, the model returns +24.3% to 31 December 2027 (+20.0% annualised; value SEK 179.49) and +38.6% to 30 June 2029 (+12.9% annualised; value SEK 200.19). The model's return template splits these into earnings (+31.7% and +42.2%), dividends (+6.2% and +9.8%) and the multiple (-10.3% and -9.4%). The negative multiple leg is a mechanical artefact of the template (see the end notes); the arithmetic that matters is that the value at each horizon equals the fair multiple times the forward earnings at that date.

The point that decides the return: the forward earnings at the first horizon do not grow. At end-2027 the two-year-forward EPS will be FY2029's SEK 8.80, in both the model and consensus (where a single broker forecasts FY2029). The two-year-forward EPS in today's price is SEK 9.06 on consensus, or about SEK 8.5 on the model's blend. The earnings step (+33% from FY2025's SEK 6.03 to FY2027's SEK 8.04, which is roughly the template's earnings leg) is real, but it is already inside the forward earnings on which the stock is priced. At an unchanged multiple, therefore, the share price in fourteen months equals today's (16.4x × SEK 8.80 = SEK 144), and the return is the dividends. Every point of return above the dividends must come from a higher multiple: the model's +24.3% is, in substance, the move from 16.4x to 19.4x.

My view of the return, to 31 December 2027. Values include dividends of SEK 9.0 to end-2027 (SEK 14.1 to mid-2029), counted as the template counts them, and returns are measured from SEK 144.40.

The probability-weighted total return to end-2027 is about zero. Over three years to mid-2029, forward EPS of about SEK 9.7 (FY2030's SEK 9.31 plus a year of mid-single-digit growth) at 15.5x gives SEK 150, plus SEK 14.1 of dividends: about +14% in total, or about +5% a year. At 19.4x the same calculation reproduces the model's +39%; at 12.9x it gives about -4%.

So-what: where the skew flips. At SEK 115 to 120 (13x to 13.5x forward earnings), the same three cases give returns of about -6%, +24% and +47%: a probability-weighted return of about +23%, with a four-to-one skew (table below). Three facts make that price plausible within twelve months: the sector's precedent for a re-rated stock meeting a margin miss (-20% to -40%), the dated negatives in H1 2027, and a share price that was at SEK 95 as recently as April 2026. The second route to a positive skew works at today's price, on evidence: contract margins of 8% or more in the February and May 2027 segment data would lift forward EPS to about SEK 9.5 and justify 16x to 17x. SEK 160 to 175 would then be the base case, and the downside case would be little worse than collecting the dividend.

Strongest counter-case. The template's higher return is the disciplined answer: it applies the rule, and the rule places the stock in the phase where multiples reach the top of the range. On consensus (FY2029 EPS of SEK 8.80, but FY2028 at SEK 9.45 on a 7.1% margin) plus a refill award, forward EPS at end-2027 could be SEK 9.5 to 10; at 17x to 19x that gives SEK 170 to 190, a return of +25% to +40%. DNB Carnegie's SEK 173 target is the public version of that case.

What would change my view. The evidence route above (segment margins showing contract margins of 8% or more), a new award in H1 2027 or a SEK 1bn distribution would move my base case to the upside row. A Finnish provision or a 51% cash-conversion print would move it to the downside row.

Score: 30. A modal return of about the dividend yield, inside a roughly symmetric range of -25% to +20%, is not the unusually positive skew Richard looks for at this price; that skew appears about 20% lower, or on one dated piece of evidence.

#13 Summary conclusion

Bravida is a good Nordic installer in its best volume year since 2022, and the market already knows it. A contracted data-centre book lifts FY2027 revenue by 11.6% and adjusted EPS by about 14%, on top of FY2026's +17%. All of that is well founded, and all of it is in consensus.

What is not well founded is the half of consensus that depends on margins. Consensus turns a package contractor's 5% to 6% margin on the data-centre work into 10%, and a 6.6% core margin into 7.0%. Those two assumptions are worth 8% to 10% of FY2027 to FY2028 EPS; they are tested only in the 2027 reports; and, on Bravida's own 2023 precedent, the test is set up to disappoint. The multiple (16.4x, the 95th percentile of two years and three and a half turns above Instalco, which offers the same Swedish recovery) is the same bet taken twice.

At today's price the most likely return is about the dividend. The forward EPS the market prices plateaus from FY2028, because the data-centre book completes faster than a two-project organisation can refill it. At my fair multiple of 15.5x, the modal fourteen-month return is therefore about the dividend, and the probability-weighted return is about zero inside a range of -25% to +20%. That is not the bet Richard is looking for.

The bet is the same business at SEK 115 to 120, or at today's price with evidence. At SEK 115 to 120 the skew is four to one. At today's price, the stock becomes a bet once the Finnish and Norwegian segment margins in February and May 2027 show the contracts earning 8% or more. The next two reports will look strong for reasons already known: use them to lighten holdings, not to add, and keep the four tests below as the live checklist. If all four pass, the gap to consensus halves and the evidence route opens early.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: B.

Two dated external forces (a lagged construction recovery and SEK 7 to 8bn of contracted data-centre work) and a completed internal clean-up give a genuine two-year EPS step, but the absence of a chief-executive change or a guidance raise, and a step that plateaus, keep the thesis out of the top decile.

Foundations' Robustness: C.

A variable cost base, a 48% indexed service franchise, the strongest balance sheet in its peer group and an above-median operating team sit on an industry that withholds price, a flat ten-year margin range, no pricing power and controls untested on turnkey work.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: C.

The case fits the “Demand-driven EPS upgrade” setup in mechanism (FY2025 to FY2027 EPS +37% on the brokers' base, driven by volume), but two-thirds of the step is in the price, the step ends in FY2028, and the chance to buy at a trough multiple of trough earnings closed at SEK 75 to 80; it is a recognisable setup that is no longer crisp.

Case Riskiness: D.

Revenue is simple and trackable, but the deciding variable, the data-centre contract margin, is unobservable until it has happened; a SEK 100 to 400m write-down is a one-in-four binary risk; FY2027 cash depends on undisclosed milestone terms; and a 95th-percentile, company-specific multiple would amplify any miss.
